title: The Same Gene, Too Much Pain

scenes.tts: Losing this channel removes pain. How could changing the same gene cause too much pain?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Same Gene, Too Much Pain. One gene cartoon with arrows running two ways: no pain, and burning pain.
scenes.narration: Losing this channel removes pain. How could changing the same gene cause too much pain?

scenes.tts: Variants in the same gene run the other way. These ones alter gating, and their channels are expressed and conducting.
scenes.visual: Two schematic panels: a loss-of-function construct giving no measurable current, and a conducting mutant with altered gating. Both labelled schematic.
scenes.narration: Variants in the same gene run the other way. These ones alter gating, and their channels are expressed and conducting.

scenes.tts: In primary erythermalgia, people have burning pain in the hands and feet.
scenes.visual: Hands and feet shaded red on a body outline. Label: primary erythermalgia.
scenes.narration: In primary erythermalgia, people have burning pain in the hands and feet.

scenes.tts: The channel protein is there. Something about its gating has gone wrong.
scenes.visual: A channel in the membrane, intact, with a question mark over its voltage sensor.
scenes.narration: The channel protein is there. Something about its gating has gone wrong.

scenes.tts: In gating terms, what would a sodium channel have to do wrong to cause too much pain?
scenes.visual: Three empty slots on screen beside a closed channel: opening, closing, inactivating.
scenes.narration: In gating terms, what would a sodium channel have to do wrong to cause too much pain?

scenes.tts: Three gating changes turn up in pain-associated variants. Open too easily, close too slowly, or fail to inactivate.
scenes.visual: The three slots fill in with small animations: an early opening, a slow closing, and a current that decays to a persistent component rather than to zero.
scenes.narration: Three gating changes turn up in pain-associated variants. Open too easily, close too slowly, or fail to inactivate.

scenes.tts: All three have been found in people, in the same gene.
scenes.visual: The three slots each gain a human-genetics tag.
scenes.narration: All three have been found in people, in the same gene.

scenes.tts: Yang and colleagues found missense variants in a family with erythermalgia, and in a sporadic patient.
scenes.visual: A pedigree with affected members, plus a single unrelated figure. Label: SCN9A missense variants.
scenes.narration: Yang and colleagues found missense variants in a family with erythermalgia, and in a sporadic patient.

scenes.tts: The next step is the one this field insists on. Take each variant into a recording rig.
scenes.visual: A variant list on the left, a patch-clamp rig on the right, an arrow between them.
scenes.narration: The next step is the one this field insists on. Take each variant into a recording rig.

scenes.tts: The recordings were made at about room temperature, where sodium-channel kinetics are slower.
scenes.visual: A thermometer beside the rig. On screen: about 21 °C, kinetics slower than at body temperature.
scenes.narration: The recordings were made at about room temperature, where sodium-channel kinetics are slower.

scenes.tts: Two of those variants were expressed in cultured cells and compared with wild type.
scenes.visual: A recording rig beside two labelled constructs. Labels: I848T, L858H, cultured cells at about 21 °C.
scenes.narration: Two of those variants were expressed in cultured cells and compared with wild type.

scenes.tts: Activation was shifted toward more negative voltages. The channel opened where it should be shut.
scenes.visual: Two activation curves: the mutant curve displaced leftward from wild type, with the resting voltage marked.
scenes.narration: Activation was shifted toward more negative voltages. The channel opened where it should be shut.

scenes.tts: Deactivation was slowed. Once open, the channel lingered.
scenes.visual: A tail current that decays slowly beside a fast wild-type tail.
scenes.narration: Deactivation was slowed. Once open, the channel lingered.

scenes.tts: A channel that opens too easily and closes too late should make its neuron easier to drive. That is an expectation from a cell line, not a recording of the neuron.
scenes.visual: The mutant channel in a nociceptor membrane, with a small stimulus and a dashed, hypothetical spike train. Tag: expectation, not recorded here.
scenes.narration: A channel that opens too easily and closes too late should make its neuron easier to drive. That is an expectation from a cell line, not a recording of the neuron.

scenes.tts: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder is a third pattern. Fast inactivation is impaired.
scenes.visual: A third trace: the current fails to decay and leaves a standing tail. Label: paroxysmal extreme pain disorder.
scenes.narration: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder is a third pattern. Fast inactivation is impaired.

scenes.tts: What is left behind is persistent sodium current, in three mutant channels tested in vitro.
scenes.visual: The trace shows a transient peak that decays onto a standing component, tinted and labelled persistent sodium current. Tag: three mutant channels, in vitro.
scenes.narration: What is left behind is persistent sodium current, in three mutant channels tested in vitro.

scenes.tts: Same gene, three distinct channel lesions, three phenotypes.
scenes.visual: Three columns: variant, gating step broken, phenotype, filled in for the three cases.
scenes.narration: Same gene, three distinct channel lesions, three phenotypes.

scenes.tts: So one gene can remove pain in one family and cause it in another.
scenes.visual: Two pedigrees side by side under one gene label, with opposite phenotype tags.
scenes.narration: So one gene can remove pain in one family and cause it in another.

scenes.tts: These gating measurements came from channels expressed in cultured cells. The pain syndromes themselves were observed and reported in people.
scenes.visual: A culture dish and a current trace on one side; on the other, a clinic icon labelled reported pain. A divider between them reads: different levels of evidence.
scenes.narration: These gating measurements came from channels expressed in cultured cells. The pain syndromes themselves were observed and reported in people.

scenes.tts: And a gating change still has to pass through the neuron before it reaches behaviour.
scenes.visual: A chain of three panels: channel, neuron, behaviour, with the neuron panel highlighted.
scenes.narration: And a gating change still has to pass through the neuron before it reaches behaviour.

scenes.tts: So the gating step tells you what the protein does. What the neuron does with that is the next film's question.
scenes.visual: An arrow from each gating step to a channel outcome: no measurable current; opens too easily; fails to inactivate. Then a second arrow, greyed and labelled depends on the neuron, toward behaviour.
scenes.narration: So the gating step tells you what the protein does. What the neuron does with that is the next film's question.

scenes.tts: A variant list is not a mechanism. The gating step is where the mechanism starts.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the gene names the protein; the gating step starts the mechanism.
scenes.narration: A variant list is not a mechanism. The gating step is where the mechanism starts.
